entities.summary: Helen Hunt Jackson was an American poet and writer who became an activist for improved treatment of Native Americans by the United States government. She described the adverse effects of government actions in her history A Century of Dishonor (1881). Her popular novel Ramona (1884) dramatized the federal government's mistreatment of Native Americans in Southern California after the Mexican–American War and attracted considerable attention to her cause. Commercially successful, it was estimated to have been reprinted 300 times, with readers liking its romantic and picturesque qualities more than its political content.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Helen Hunt Jackson's works, particularly A Century of Dishonor and Ramona, drew attention to the mistreatment of Native Americans by the US government, influencing public opinion and contributing to the passage of the Dawes Act in 1887.
